standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness means the tensor functor is exact
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Modules on Sites, definition of flat module
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that \mathcal{G} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_1} - is exact, hence so is the isomorphic functor (\mathcal{G} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_1} \mathcal{O}_2) \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_2} -.

core_obligations: Display the change-of-rings identity (\mathcal{G} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_1} \mathcal{O}_2) \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_2} \mathcal{H} = \mathcal{G} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_1} \mathcal{H} as sheaves of abelian groups (proof lines 4837-4840).

Conclude that (\mathcal{G} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_1} \mathcal{O}_2) \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_2} - is exact because \mathcal{G} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_1} - is, so the extension of scalars is a flat \mathcal{O}_2-module (proof lines 4841-4844).
proof_roadmap: Identify tensoring the extension of scalars with tensoring over the base ring.
Invoke flatness of \mathcal{G} over \mathcal{O}_1 to conclude exactness over \mathcal{O}_2.
difficulty_reason: The proof displays the change-of-rings identity (\mathcal{G} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_1} \mathcal{O}_2) \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_2} \mathcal{H} = \mathcal{G} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_1} \mathcal{H} (as sheaves of abelian groups, for example), by which tensoring over \mathcal{O}_2 with \mathcal{H} against the extension of scalars is the same functor as tensoring over \mathcal{O}_1 with \mathcal{H} — exact in \mathcal{H} because \mathcal{G} is \mathcal{O}_1-flat. The displayed identity is the complete derivation; the author's verbatim text writes \mathcal{F} for the right-hand module (an arbitary test module), delivered as-is.
